purpose: Editorial review ledger; never imported as approved production items

items.stem: There are three clubs, but I can join only one. I need to ___ which one I like best.

options.rationale: Describing does not select one club.
Selects one option from several.
Visiting is not deciding which to join.
Explaining does not select one.

blocking_risks: Only one and one club strongly cue selection; may be a low-difficulty anchor.

items.stem: The shop sells the same notebook for £3.50, but the one next door charges £4. What is the shop's ___ for the notebook?

options.rationale: Weight is how heavy an item is, not the amount charged.
Price is the amount a shop charges.
Size is the item's dimensions, not the amount charged.
Colour is an appearance property, not the amount charged.

blocking_risks: No second key found in this pass, but distractors are very easy and the £ figures directly cue money; likely only an A1 anchor.

items.stem: The school would like parents to come to a meeting on Thursday. It will ___ them by sending a message asking them to attend.

options.rationale: An invitation asks someone to attend an event.
A reminder assumes parents already know about the event or arrangement.
Informing communicates facts but does not necessarily request attendance.
Thanking expresses gratitude, not an attendance request.

blocking_risks: Inform may also be a reasonable description of sending a message; stem and key definition strongly overlap. HOLD for independent review.

items.stem: I know you agreed to bring the books tomorrow. I'll ___ you again before you leave home.

options.rationale: An invitation asks someone to join an event, not recall an agreement.
Warning alerts someone to danger or an unwanted consequence, not simply an existing agreement.
Contacting describes reaching someone, but not the purpose of recalling the agreement.
Reminding brings an earlier agreement back to mind.

blocking_risks: Contact is possible as an action, but less precise than remind; test whether 'again' and prior agreement make this too easy.

items.stem: The school shortened lunch breaks. One unexpected ___ was that fewer students attended lunchtime clubs.

options.rationale: An intention is an aim, not the resulting lower attendance.
A proposal is a suggested plan, not the result.
A requirement is an obligation, not the outcome.
A consequence is a result of an action.

blocking_risks: Three distractors are semantically distant; needs better matched alternatives.

items.stem: The equipment is not the best available, but it is ___ for the basic tasks we need to complete.

options.rationale: Means sufficient for the specified purpose.
Implies unusually high quality, not merely sufficient.
Means more than necessary, not sufficient.
Means inappropriate for the tasks.

blocking_risks: Distractors are weakly matched and may be eliminated by polarity.

items.stem: The researcher avoided calling the programme simply a success or a failure. Instead, she offered a ___ assessment that considered differences between student groups.

options.rationale: Decisive suggests a firm judgement, not careful distinctions.
Uniform implies sameness, at odds with group differences.
Recognises subtle differences and qualified interpretations.
Superficial lacks detailed consideration.

blocking_risks: Stem explicitly explains the target; possible low discrimination at C1.

items.stem: The school sent so many homework reminders that students stopped checking notifications. Late submissions rose from 10% to 25%, although the aim was to reduce them. The policy was ___.

options.rationale: The measure worsened the problem it was intended to solve.
The policy did not achieve its aim, but this is also true when it worsens the outcome: potentially defensible.
The reminders might have been unnecessary, but this is not established by the data.
Student attitudes are not directly measured.

blocking_risks: Ineffective remains technically true even when the policy is counterproductive; a 'best' instruction might distinguish precision, but the second key remains defensible. BLOCKED pending a different distractor.

notes: Revision v3 addresses grammatical mismatch and some second-key risks; explicit unresolved ambiguities remain. Editorial self-review is not independent approval.
